record.what_it_does: All-in-one workspace for notes, docs, databases and project management.
record.auth_notes: Internal connection token (static, one workspace), personal access token (acts as a user), and OAuth 2.0 for public/scoped integrations (access and refresh tokens). Each user authorizes individually and picks pages to share. Multi-user toolkits use OAuth with a public integration.
record.access_notes: Docs say OAuth can begin once client credentials and a redirect URI are configured, and "Marketplace submission or review is not required". Creating an internal connection needs a workspace owner. I did not find a pricing page confirming the API is available on the free plan. The Notion MCP token needs a Business or Enterprise plan, but that is a separate path.
record.api_breadth_notes: Base URL api.notion.com, versioned with a Notion-Version header. Covers pages, databases/data sources, blocks, comments, users, search and file uploads. I did not count operations. The docs publish an llms.txt index.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.notion.com/mcp (hosted by Notion, documented on developers.notion.com). It uses OAuth by default. Business and Enterprise plans can also use a bearer MCP token.
record.blocker_notes: Public OAuth integrations need no marketplace review. Users must select the pages they share with the integration. A free Notion workspace can be used for testing, but I did not confirm this from the docs.

evidence.quote: Marketplace submission or review is not required.
public integrations can be installed in any workspace
Notion will tell you the moment something important happens.

record.needs_human: Confirm that the API is free on the free Notion plan. Confirm whether an OpenAPI spec exists, since I did not find one. Confirm whether a sandbox exists. The fetch results are summaries, so the quotes are paraphrase-adjacent and worth spot-checking.
